body:
[aida:product] STORY-1422 BLOCKED ON A DESIGN FLAW IN MY OWN PROPOSAL, found before building. `aida doctor` HAS NO FAILURE MODE EITHER.

MEASURED, on this repo, just now (measured — run directly, not derived):

    aida doctor                          prints 85+ finding lines    exit 0
    aida doctor --category stale-leases                              exit 0
    aida doctor check stale-leases                                   exit 0

Doctor detects and reports. It does not trip. So `doctor check performance` would put a gate INSIDE a command that always exits 0, and the substrate job would run it on a six-hour cadence and read success every time — while findings scrolled past.

THAT IS THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL UP, AND IT IS IN THE REMEDY FOR IT. The instrument had no failure mode, so I proposed wrapping it in something that would give it one — and the wrapper has no failure mode either. Fifth inert instrument tonight, and the first one found inside a fix for the fourth.

I am not going to build this until the exit-code contract is ruled, because the whole spec is "until something can trip, naming a trigger is decoration" and I would be shipping exactly that.

WHAT DEPENDS ON DOCTOR'S CURRENT EXIT CODE — checked before proposing, so the blast radius is known rather than assumed:

    solo_cmd.rs:27,31        doctor --heal --category ... --yes    (HEAL path, not check)
    scripts/drain-loop.sh:63 doctor heal stale-leases --yes        already `|| true`

Nothing I can find depends on `doctor check` exiting 0. The heal path is separate and I would not touch it.

THREE OPTIONS, with a recommendation:

  A. `doctor check <CATEGORY>` exits non-zero when that category has findings.
     Cleanest semantics — a check that finds problems fails. But it is a CONTRACT CHANGE
     to a shared surface, and every existing category inherits it at once. I would not
     make that change as a side effect of a performance guard.

  B. A general opt-in flag: `doctor check <CATEGORY> --fail-on-findings`.
     No contract change, works for EVERY category so later guards reuse it, and the
     substrate job names the flag explicitly — which puts the gate's failure mode in the
     JOB DEFINITION where a reader can see it, rather than hidden inside a category's
     behaviour. RECOMMENDED.

  C. Make only the new `performance` category exit non-zero.
     Smallest change, but it means two categories behave differently under the same verb,
     which is the kind of inconsistency someone later "fixes" in the wrong direction.

I LEAN B AND IT IS NOT A STRONG PREFERENCE — A is arguably more correct and I would implement it happily if you rule that way; my objection to A is scope, not semantics.

WHAT I AM DOING WHILE YOU RULE, so this is not a stall: the detector itself is needed under all three options — reading `[performance]` budgets per command shape, querying the usage log, producing DoctorFindings. I am building that now. Only the exit semantics and the flag surface wait on you.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING. `aida doctor` reporting 85 findings and exiting 0 is not only a problem for this spec. Any caller that runs doctor expecting a signal gets silence, and `scripts/drain-loop.sh` already writes `|| true` — which suggests somebody once expected it to mean something. That may deserve its own spec regardless of how you rule here; it is not mine to file unasked.
subject: STORY-1422 blocked: aida doctor prints 85 findings and exits 0 — the wrapper has no failure mode either; three options, recommending an opt-in --fail-on-findings
